subject: Engineering Technology
question: Which of the following are real engineering applications of Artificial Intelligence? (Select all correct answers.)
options: Predictive maintenance on factory turbines using sensor streams
Computer vision quality inspection on semiconductor wafers
Automated medical imaging triage assisting clinicians
Suspending conservation of energy in physical engines

explanation.why: AI excels at pattern detection in sensor telemetry, high-speed optical defect detection, and diagnostic imaging—while still obeying physical laws.
explanation.shortcut: AI optimizes prediction, vision, and control; it cannot violate physics.
explanation.commonTrap: AI assists engineers with data and optimization—it does not break physics laws.

subject: Engineering Technology
question: What does CAD stand for in mechanical, civil, and architectural engineering?

explanation.why: CAD (Computer-Aided Design) software lets engineers model 2D blueprints and 3D assemblies precisely before fabrication.
explanation.commonTrap: Don't confuse CAD (design modeling) with CAM (Computer-Aided Manufacturing).

subject: Engineering Technology
question: Why does an autonomous drone often run obstacle-avoidance inference on an onboard edge processor rather than sending every frame to a remote cloud server?
options: Edge processing minimizes network latency and continues working if wireless connectivity drops
Cloud data centers cannot perform matrix multiplication
Edge chips weigh more and consume infinite battery power intentionally
Wireless latency is zero milliseconds across global servers

explanation.why: Safety-critical robotics needs millisecond latency and resilience against signal dropouts, making local edge compute essential.
explanation.shortcut: Real-time safety/robotics -> Edge compute for ultra-low latency.
explanation.commonTrap: Cloud is great for heavy training, but real-time flight control needs local inference.
